text: Three studies are summarized. High-resolution sperm typing of the mouse MHC E(beta) gene confirms a highly localized 1.0–1.6 kb hotspot in the second intron, flanked by recombinationally inert DNA. Crossover rate varies by haplotype but the hotspot is constant; reciprocal orientations show different distributions with centre points shifted ~400 bp on average, causing biased gene conversion favouring non-initiating haplotype markers, supporting the double-strand break repair model with haplotype s as the most efficient initiator—strikingly similar to human hotspots. Second, CBP and p300 KIX domains interact genetically with c-Myb; the CBP KIX mutation affects platelets, B cells, T cells and red cells only when combined with a p300 KIX mutation, contributing to c-Myb-dependent activation and repression required for hematopoiesis. Third, Tet1 is dispensable for pluripotency, its loss compatible with embryonic and postnatal development.
